findings.title: nextPreReleaseVersion() treats identifier "0" as non-numeric and appends instead of incrementing
findings.property: with no ids, the last numeric identifier of the pre-release is incremented by one
findings.evidence: Javadoc: 'the current pre-release version's last numeric identifier is incremented'. "0" is a valid numeric identifier per SemVer, but private isNumeric() returns false for any id starting with "0", including "0" itself.

review.title: nextPreReleaseVersion() appends ".1" instead of incrementing when the last pre-release identifier is "0"
review.reason: In Version.java, `isNumeric` returns false for any identifier starting with "0", including "0" itself, which SemVer defines as a valid numeric identifier. `incrementIdentifiers` therefore treats `1.0.0-alpha.0` as having a non-numeric last id and gives `1.0.0-alpha.0.1`, which contradicts the Javadoc ('last numeric identifier is incremented'). The check was clearly meant to exclude only leading-zero forms like "01", which the parser rejects anyway. The same flaw affects `compareIdentifiers`, where "0" is compared as a string. A fix is a one-line change, to `id.equals("0") || !id.startsWith("0")`.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code

findings.title: compareToIgnoreBuildMetadata orders numeric identifier above alphanumeric identifier starting with '-'
findings.property: a numeric pre-release identifier always has lower precedence than an alphanumeric one
findings.actual: 1.0.0-1 compares greater than 1.0.0--a (ASCII string comparison, '-' < digits)
findings.evidence: Javadoc says the method adheres to the Specification's comparison rules; SemVer 2.0.0 item 11: 'Numeric identifiers always have lower precedence than non-numeric identifiers.' Identifiers may contain '-' ([0-9A-Za-z-]), but compareIdentifiers falls back to String.compareTo when one side is non-numeric.

review.title: compareToIgnoreBuildMetadata ranks numeric pre-release identifiers above alphanumeric ones that start with '-'
review.reason: `1.0.0--a` is valid SemVer, since identifiers may contain '-'. SemVer item 11 says numeric identifiers always rank below non-numeric ones. `compareIdentifiers` (Version.java:1331-1337) falls back to `String.compareTo` whenever either side is non-numeric, and '-' (0x2D) sorts before digits, so `1.0.0-1` compares greater than `1.0.0--a`. Digits sort before every other legal identifier character, so only identifiers starting with '-' are affected. A fix is small: if exactly one identifier is numeric, return -1 for the numeric one and 1 for the other. Related: `isNumeric` returns false for "0", so `1.0.0-0` vs `1.0.0--x` is also wrong.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code
